glosses: To bring (someone) into the presence of (a person); to introduce formally.

examples.text: to present an envoy to the king

glosses: To nominate (a member of the clergy) for an ecclesiastical benefice; to offer to the bishop or ordinary as a candidate for institution.
To offer (a problem, complaint) to a court or other authority for consideration.
To charge (a person) with a crime or accusation; to bring before court.

examples.text: In the diocese of Gloucester in 1548 two inhabitants of Slimbridge were presented for saying that holy oil was ‘of no virtue but meet to grease sheep’.

glosses: To come forward, appear in a particular place or before a particular person, especially formally.

examples.text: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the lord.

glosses: To put (something) forward in order for it to be seen; to show, exhibit.

examples.text: So ladies in romance assist their knight, / Present the spear, and arm him for the fight.
Note: The offensive team must present a legal formation both before and after a shift.

glosses: To make clear to one's mind or intelligence; to put forward for consideration.

examples.text: I do begin to realize that the matter must be presented in such a way as may interest the reader.

glosses: To put on, stage (a play etc.).

examples.text: The theater is proud to present the Fearless Fliers.

glosses: To point (a firearm) at something, to hold (a weapon) in a position ready to fire.
To offer oneself for mental consideration; to occur to the mind.

examples.text: Well, one idea does present itself.

glosses: To come to the attention of medical staff, especially with a specific symptom.

examples.text: The patient presented with insomnia.
Symptoms typically present in early childhood.

glosses: To appear (in a specific way) for delivery (of a fetus); to appear first at the mouth of the uterus during childbirth.

examples.text: At that time, Elbe was presenting as a man.

glosses: To act as presenter on (a radio, television programme etc.).

examples.text: Anne Robinson presents "The Weakest Link".

glosses: To give a gift or presentation to (someone).

examples.text: She was presented with an honorary degree for her services to entertainment.

glosses: To give (a gift or presentation) to someone; to bestow.

examples.text: Live thou, and reign, forever, glorious Lord! / My last, least off’ring, I present thee now— / Renounce me, leave me, and be still ador’d! / Slay me, my God, and I applaud the blow.

glosses: To deliver (something abstract) as though as a gift; to offer.

glosses: To hand over (a bill etc.) to be paid.
